transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I'm here because I just can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work at a dry cleaner, and lately, it's just a mess. I've got tickets, receipts, workshop notes, and customer jobs all piled together. It gets to the point where I just look at it all and I don't even know what to handle first. It's really starting to become a problem.
Have you struggled with organization and focus since you were a child, or is this a new problem for you?

No, it's not a new problem at all. It's been this way since I was little. Even back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was a bright kid, but just really scattered. I was always talking out of turn in class, losing my papers, and needing constant reminders just to finish my work. So, yeah, it's been a struggle my whole life.
Nowadays, do you often feel restless, fidgety, or like you constantly need to be on the move?

I don't really think so. I mean, I'm on my feet most of the day at the shop anyway, moving between the racks and the counter, so... I haven't really noticed feeling restless. I don't get that feeling like I constantly need to be moving, no.
Do these difficulties with focus and organization also cause problems for you at home or in your personal life?

Yeah, it really does. At the shop, it's not just a messy counter—we've had late orders and confused billing because of it. It's definitely caused some tense moments with the other staff and the customers lately. And outside of work... well, at my church, I actually had to step back from leading some of the event planning. People were just getting frustrated with me because I couldn't keep things straight, so I had to let it go.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of executive dysfunction, disorganization, and feeling overwhelmed at work suggests inattentive ADHD, a depressive or anxiety disorder, early cognitive impairment, or an adjustment disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a long-standing history of severe disorganization, difficulty managing tasks, losing materials, and requiring reminders to finish work dating back to childhood (grade school). These symptoms result in significant functional impairment across multiple domains (occupational difficulties at the dry cleaner and social/community role impairments at church).
